messages:
alex_wei: Heads-up — onboarding a small pilot (acct 123456789012) next week. Need p5 + g5 capacity in eu-west-7 for E2E tests. Can someone kick off quota/entitlement?

samira: What exactly do you need (instance types + counts, ENIs, launch window)?

alex_wei: p5.48xlarge: 2, p4d.24xlarge: 1, g5.48xlarge: 4. Expect ~30 ENIs across instances. Preferred launch 2024-11-05. AMI/drivers handled by infra image team.

liam_ops: FYI eu-west-7 is relatively new; AWS treats accelerator entitlements separate from Service Quotas. I'll open a Business Support case + Service Quotas requests. Please confirm account alias/org unit.

alex_wei: Account alias: redwood-pilot-eu7, AWS ID 123456789012. Tagging: pilot:true, cost-center:pilot-eu7. Expected steady usage ~200 GPU-hours/day during pilot.

liam_ops: Opening case now. infra-bot: created support case #CASE-987654321 and submitted Service Quotas for p5/p4d/g5 OnDemand. Also requested ENI limit bump to 500. Link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=CASE-987654321

infra-bot: (automated) Business justification required: "Pilot to validate Redwood inference on p5/g5 for customer workload. Production-like load, launch date 2024-11-05. Need sustained, non-spot capacity."

samira: Subnet sizing question: our eu-west-7 core subnets are /20 (~400 addrs) — might be tight if other services expand. We can carve a dedicated /19 but that needs coord with networking. liam_ops, can you check?

liam_ops: I'll check available IP space. Carving /19 is doable but a follow-up. For now raising ENI limit avoids immediate block.

alex_wei: If AWS denies entitlement, fallback regions? Data residency might block non-eu-west-7.

liam_ops: Fallback = eu-west-6 (less preferred). Note cost differences and cross-region latency. Finance ok with pilot spend?

samira: Finance flagged cost — suggest getting a reserved-capacity quote if steady. For pilot, avoid spot (need stable perf).

liam_ops: Noted in the case: "No spot, need reserved-like availability for pilot window." infra-bot: uploaded initial billing estimate to case.

aws_support: AWS Support: routed accelerator entitlement to regional capacity team. ETA for first response 48–72 hrs. Please supply projected monthly GPU-hours per instance type.

alex_wei: Monthly projection: p5: 150 hrs/month, p4d: 80 hrs/month, g5: 300 hrs/month. Also request ENI bump to 500 and increase for VPC prefix limits.

samira: Do we need EFA for p4d NCCL/collectives? If yes, request EFA enablement.

liam_ops: Yes, request EFA + ENA for p4d. I'll add that to the support case and Service Quotas entries.

infra-bot: (automated) Case #CASE-987654321 updated. Support agent assigned: Rita (Capacity). Next steps: validate monthly hours and confirm no public IP requirement.

alex_wei: Confirm: Instances will not have public IPv4; we use NAT. Also need IAM role "redwood-pilot-ecs" and KMS key access for model artifacts.

liam_ops: I'll create the IAM role and add KMS policy. samira, please prepare the security checklist and run the tag/alerting playbook for cost watches.

samira: On it. I'll add cloudwatch billing alarms and a slack alert to #costs. Also will document tagging policy: cost-center:pilot-eu7, team:platform.

aws_support: Agent Rita: Received projections. We're validating capacity. If approved, we'll issue entitlement code and update Service Quotas. If region capacity constrained, we'll propose phased allocation.

liam_ops: If phased, request priority allocation: p5 > p4d > g5. p5s are critical for the benchmark numbers.

alex_wei: Thanks — keep this thread updated. Any estimate lead time difference between entitlement (fast) vs Dedicated reserved pool?

samira: Dedicated reserved pool typically 2–6 weeks depending on region and capacity. Entitlement sometimes 2–3 days if available.

infra-bot: (automated) Please attach business justification doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/pilot-eu7-justification

liam_ops: I'll post updates here once Rita responds. If anyone hears anything from AWS directly, ping @liam_ops.

alex_wei: Cheers — appreciate the fast turnaround."
